sources: Penn State Extension, Cluster Flies: "These flies are not reproducing within the structure, but become active on warm days and crawl out of wall voids and attics in a confused attempt to go back outside."; "the flies will gather in large numbers at windows within the home on warm winter days. The flies are typically sluggish in flight"; "Adult cluster flies are slightly larger than the common house fly... They are dull gray with black markings and have golden-yellow hairs on the thorax, which can give the appearance of a golden sheen."; "Although insecticidal dust treatments to these voids may kill thousands of flies..."; https://extension.psu.edu/cluster-flies

Colorado State University Extension, Cluster Flies and Other Winter Flies: "Cluster flies found in buildings are in a dormant state and cannot reproduce indoors."; "Cluster flies develop by feeding on earthworms."; "cluster flies then find sheltered areas in wall voids or attics where they may aggregate"; https://extension.colostate.edu/resource/cluster-flies-and-other-winter-flies/

beats.say: Thousands of flies can sleep inside your walls.
One warm day wakes them. They crawl out.
They crowd your sunny windows, dazed and sluggish.
Slightly bigger than house flies, with golden hairs.
They can't breed in your house.
Their babies grow inside earthworms, outdoors.
They're just lost, not nesting. Right now,
